text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT PAGER -> severity: P1. Serving cluster 'us-west-2-gpu' high RDMA retransmit rate > 12% detected. Error class: IB_RETRANS_THRESHOLD. Affected service: runtime-serving.

len: paging oncall. i'm looking. seeing a sudden spike in packet retransmits to rack 7.

maria: oncall taking. can you dump the node list with high retransmits?

len: quick grep: `for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l rack=7 -o name); do echo $n; done` shows node-7-01, node-7-02. both show e10k retransmit counters high.

emma: logs from runtime show repeated RPC stalls and goroutines backing up, KV cache growth, then containers getting OOMKilled. stack traces include blocked net/dial timeouts followed by big allocation spikes.

raj: that fits — when RDMA stalls, our serving pipeline holds buffers and tokens accumulate. we hit device memory while waiting on remote responses. immediate mitigations: reduce max-parallel-requests and enable fallback to tcp for new connections.

ops-sre: agree. can we throttle ingress for these nodes and route traffic away?

len: starting traffic rampdown for rack 7. routing rule change:
```
# route away from rack 7
kubectl annotate svc runtime-serving routing-priority=low --overwrite
kubectl label nodes node-7-01 cordoned=true
kubectl label nodes node-7-02 cordoned=true
```

maria: cordon + drain pods with 5m grace. running `kubectl drain node-7-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` now. will move pods to other racks.

deploy-bot: deploy started: traffic-fallback/tcp-enabled @ 2087660105.

emma: after routing change, error rate on serving decreased from 18% -> 6% in the next 3 minutes, but latency tail (p99) is still high for chat endpoints. some containers still OOMing during inflight requests.

raj: for residual OOMs, kill looped tasks and restart the runtime process with reduced batch size. command to update config map: 
```
kubectl patch configmap/runtime-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"8","batch_window_ms":"5"}}'
```

len: executed patch at 2087660700. restarted runtime replicas on the two worst nodes.

ops-sre: ethernet counters on node-7-02 show 1.2M RX errors and multiple IB link resets. looks like the NIC firmware on that host started dropping frames.

maria: can we soft-reset NIC before hardware team escalates? manual command to reset mlx5 gracefully: 
```
# on affected host
systemctl stop rdma.service
modprobe -r mlx5_core mlx5_ib
modprobe mlx5_core mlx5_ib
systemctl start rdma.service
```

emma: be careful — that will tear down active RDMA connections. but we've already routed most traffic away. proceed on node-7-02, and keep node-7-01 cordoned until we verify link stability.

len: initiated NIC reset on node-7-02 at 2087661500. host came back, IB path probes improved. retransmit rate dropped to 2.5% but we still saw intermittent spikes.

ops-sre: firmware mismatch log entry found: `mlx5_fw: unexpected version 34.1` — scheduling a firmware roll forward with hardware team, but that is not immediate.

raj: to avoid recurrence we should enable connection-level graceful fallback to TCP for RKD endpoints when retransmit > 3% threshold. add a runtime flag: `--rdma-fallback-threshold=0.03`.

maria: applying runtime flag via deployment patch now.

deploy-bot: runtime-flag rollout started @ 2087662400. Canary on 10% of replicas.

product-ops: are customers impacted? we need a short blurb for comms.

emma: customer impact summary for comms: ~6% overall request errors during 2087659999-2087662000 window. P99 latency increased to ~1.8s (normal 0.6s) for chat endpoints during peak. No data loss, requests retried by clients; some sessions had transient failures.

len: posting interim status to status page: 
- incident detected: 2087659999
- partial mitigation: rerouted traffic and enabled TCP fallback 2087660105
- residual errors reduced to ~2-3% by 2087662400

maria: handing off to len for night oncall at 2087663000. len: you're now oncall for the incident. please keep monitoring fabric counters and confirm firmware schedule. :thumbsup:

len: ack oncall. continuing watch. i set alerts: rdma_retransmit_rate > 3% and container OOM rate spike. paging thresholds restored. will coordinate firmware window with hw-team tomorrow.

ops-sre: quick postmortem TODOs (capture now):
- capture IB counters and packetdump from node-7-01/02 (`tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/ib-dump.pcap`), stash in incident bucket.
- firmware upgrade plan for mlx5 on rack 7.
- add runtime config to auto-fallback to TCP when retransmit threshold exceeded.
- add bulk-request backpressure to prevent KV cache growth from blocked RPCs.
- improve canary for firmware+driver changes.

raj: also add stress test to CI for simulated RDMA packet loss to validate fallback behavior.

product-ops: will draft customer note: short incident summary + mitigation + no data loss. will share for review.

maria: final note: we saw several containers OOM while blocked on remote fetches — mitigation of avoiding large bursts and routing away buys us time but root cause is NIC/firmware instability. hardware team owning firmware remediation. ops-sre to own final postmortem.

len: logging an incident ticket: INC-2087659999. assigning ops-sre for postmortem, raj for runtime changes, hw-team for firmware.

emma: adding logs and traces to the ticket. uploading `runtime-oom-stack.log` and `ib-counters-2087661600.csv`.

deploy-bot: rollout completed to 100% @ 2087663500. RDMA fallback enabled cluster-wide.

len: marking this thread as active but mitigated. will update when firmware window confirmed.

maria: thanks all, great triage. handing off incident followups to morning shift. :heart:

len: thread closed for live pager, leaving action items in INC-2087659999.
